title: An artificial motor protein that walks along a DNA track
authors: Patrik Nilsson; Neil O. Robertson; Nils Gustafsson; Roberta B. Davies; Chu Wai Liew; Aaron Lyons; Ralf Eichhorn; Cassandra S. Niman; Gerhard A. Blab; Elizabeth H.C. Bromley; Andrew E. Whitten; Anthony P. Duff; Ivan N. Unksov; Jason P. Beech; Peter Jönsson; Till Böcking; Birte Höcker; Derek N. Woolfson; Nancy R. Forde; Heiner Linke; Paul M. G. Curmi
one_liner_zh: 该文构建了一种沿DNA轨道定向行走的人工马达蛋白Tumbleweed，其核心依赖配体门控的DNA结合域与DNA特定位点的选择性互作，虽非典型TF-DNA体系，但蛋白质-DNA结合识别与动态行走机制对TF-DNA互作建模具有方法学借鉴价值。
abstract: Paragraph Molecular motors are fundamental to life 1–6 because of their ability to convert chemical energy into mechanical work, an ability that is conferred by the chemical and structural complexity of their constituent proteins. Scientists have long sought to create artificial protein motors that may reveal insights into how biological motors function. While artificial molecular motors based on small molecules 7 and DNA 8,9 have been developed, creating an artificial motor protein has remained an elusive goal in synthetic biology 10 . Here we demonstrate the realization of an artificial protein motor called Tumbleweed (TW) that walks directionally along a DNA track under external control. TW consists of three legs, each with a ligand-gated DNA-binding domain that enables selective interaction with specific sites along a DNA track 11 . Using single-molecule fluorescence assays and a programmable microfluidic device, we show that TW steps directionally along a designed DNA track in response to a defined sequence of ligand inputs. We built our TW molecular walker using a modular approach, combining existing proteins with known properties to achieve emergent motor function, similar to how Nature evolves new proteins. Our design strategy thus offers a a platform for engineering advanced and dynamic protein functionality. Our demonstration of TW walking represents a step toward developing fully autonomous protein motors and opens new avenues for uncovering and leveraging the principles by which biological motors transduce chemical energy into motion.
abstract_zh: 段落 分子马达是生命的基础1-6，因为它们能够将化学能转化为机械功，这一能力由其组成蛋白质的化学和结构复杂性赋予。科学家长期以来一直寻求创造人工蛋白质马达，这可能揭示生物马达如何运作的见解。虽然基于小分子7和DNA 8,9的人工分子马达已被开发，但创造人工马达蛋白在合成生物学10中仍是一个难以实现的目标。在此，我们展示了一种名为Tumbleweed (TW)的人工蛋白质马达的实现，它在外部控制下沿DNA轨道定向行走。TW由三条腿组成，每条腿具有配体门控的DNA结合域，能够与DNA轨道11上的特定位点选择性相互作用。利用单分子荧光测定和可编程微流控装置，我们表明TW在响应特定配体输入序列时，沿设计好的DNA轨道定向步进。我们采用模块化方法构建了TW分子步行器，结合具有已知特性的现有蛋白质以实现涌现的马达功能，类似于自然界进化出新蛋白质的方式。因此，我们的设计策略为工程化高级和动态蛋白质功能提供了一个平台。TW行走的演示代表了向开发全自主蛋白质马达迈出的一步，并为揭示和利用生物马达将化学能转化为运动的原理开辟了新途径。
